description: GET /runs/{id}/files restarts stopped sandbox container of terminal runs: run_files.rs reconnect_run_sandbox() calls sandbox.activate() unconditionally; DockerSandbox::activate() docker-starts the container; nothing stops it -> one leaked running container per visited finished run. Same in handler/sandbox.rs list_sandbox_files and sessions.rs. Terminal WS activate is intentional.
resolution: Unresolved; seed fabro-52f2 carries fix options (checkpoint/final_patch for terminal runs, ref-counted auto-stop, or refuse activate on terminal runs; degraded final_patch path already proven viable)

description: GET /api/v1/runs/{id}/files calls reconnect_for_run() + sandbox.activate() (run_files.rs:1216-1220). DockerSandbox::activate() docker-starts a stopped run container (docker.rs:1663, ContainerStartAction::Start) to read workspace files. No production code path in fabro-server calls .stop() afterwards (zero .stop() call sites outside workflow-engine run finalization). Browsing the Files tab of a finished run resurrects its container permanently until manual docker rm or system prune. Observed 2026-08-21: runs 01M0GG56PQYP and 01M0GJVW659C stopped correctly ~1.4s after completion on 2026-08-20 (21:10Z/21:57Z), resurrected 08:04:35Z/08:05:52Z by web UI file inspection, stayed Up ~35min until manual docker rm. Tracked as seed fabro-284b.
resolution: Open: fix directions are (a) serve file listing from checkpoint git storage, (b) stop-after-read when inspection started the container, or (c) idle reaper for containers of terminal-state runs. Seed fabro-284b.

name: sandbox-inspection-lifecycle-ownership
description: Sandbox lifecycle ownership rule: Sandbox::activate() returns SandboxActivation::{AlreadyActive,Started}. Read-only inspection endpoints wrap the sandbox in an InspectionSandbox guard (run_files.rs) that stops it again via finish() only when activation==Started AND the run status is_terminal(); interactive endpoints (terminal, SSH, file PUT) intentionally keep resurrect-on-use. This prevents web-UI browsing of finished runs from leaking running containers forever (fixed fc6accada, seed fabro-284b). When adding new inspection endpoints, always use reconnect_run_sandbox_for_inspection + finish() on every exit path (including error and degraded-fallback branches).

name: runner-image-as-config-lab-validated
description: image.dockerfile = { path = ... } on provider=docker auto-builds fabro-runner-<sha12> with inspect-first reuse (fabro-969f, runs 01M0RAB7Z3S1DZ124Z8HQGHXPN cold 89.4s / 01M0RAFNKSW0MBT2C2WM6Z2CJG reuse 43ms, setup 899ms vs 24.5s mise). Lab form: .fabro/Dockerfile.mise with mise use -g (NOT mise install — shims need version defaults without a config file), tools mirrored from .mise.toml because the build context is empty.

Environments-API stored envs (image.docker) merge with project image.dockerfile of the same id -> both-set resolve error blocked every dockerfile run; Option::combine leaked the lower layer. CLI hides the cause behind 'failed to resolve manifest settings'.
resolution: EnvironmentImageLayer hand-implements Combine: higher layer setting either field suppresses the other (commit ea08ce4b8). Reproduce pattern: fabro-manifest build_run_manifest test over a stored-catalog EnvironmentLayer.

name: engine-condition-evaluation
description: Edge conditions: parser (fabro-graphviz condition.rs) accepts dotted keys + numeric ops (>= <= > <) natively; the EVALUATOR (fabro-workflow condition.rs lookup_flat) needed dotted-path object walking — literal key first (dotted user keys keep exact match), then decompose and walk nested JSON objects; context.-prefixed variant also resolves. Routing precedence: conditional edges > preferred_label on unconditional > unconditional. Exit-kind precedence: edge kind attr > exit-node kind attr > natural. HookContext carries context_updates (journal bridge, fabro-31b2) for stage_complete AND stage_failed; sandbox hooks get context via stdin (host) or FABRO_HOOK_CONTEXT file (sandboxed); scripts CANNOT read run context — read the tracker/sd instead.

title: Sandbox disposal is a server-side retention policy, container-only, fork is the recovery path
rationale: Prod filled 188GB/503GB in 2.5 days with exited run containers (2026-09-16, prod). Engine stops but never removes sandboxes on Docker; Daytona has provider timers, Docker deliberately none. A server supervisor (not engine-at-completion, not host cron) owns reaping: terminal runs only, default 48h, budget ceiling as brake; never non-terminal/paused/HITL/preserve runs; run data (records, timeline, artifacts, scratch) never deleted — user directive. Reaped = stale-evidence run (existing glossary term): revisor disqualifies via sandbox_available, in-place resume gets actionable 'fork this run' error; fork already re-materializes from checkpoint SHA + clone coordinates, so recovery from run data exists without new engine semantics. Deferred follow-up: on-resume re-materialization (fabro-0722).

name: scoped-sandbox-decorator
description: fabro-ba96 (b312459b4): per-node filesystem scope fs_hide/fs_write enforced by a ScopedSandbox decorator wrapping the stage session's Arc<dyn Sandbox> at workflow session construction (next to node.tools()). Covers every file tool in every vocabulary, read_many_files and apply_patch for free; subagent factory gets the same wrap (inheritance). Nonexistent semantics: hidden = reads fail, file_exists false, grep/glob/list_dir/walk_files filtered, writes denied; a dir/** glob also hides the dir entry (pure-glob semantics would leak the directory through listings). apply_patch pre-checks all target paths via ToolContext.fs_scope (atomic reject, no partial application). delegate_sandbox! cannot skip overridden methods — the impl is hand-written; macro evolution only when a second decorator appears (seed 922f).

title: gh verboten in Agent-Sandboxen: ADR-0019 Capability Gate
rationale: gh was briefly baked into the toolchain image (PR #53, fabro-05d0) and REVERTED (f00fdb102, user decision 2026-09-08). Why gh is FORBIDDEN in agent sandboxes: the engine injects a freshly minted GITHUB_TOKEN into every agent shell call (fabro-workflow services.rs resolve_workflow_env) plus a git credential bridge (git_bridge.rs credential helper reads $GITHUB_TOKEN at invocation time). gh + that token = fully write-capable forge client in agent shells (merge, close, force-push, branch delete) bypassing every engine governance control (gate, revisor, auto-merge). fabro-github (server-side crate) is the ONLY sanctioned forge write path - agents express intent via mediated tools (fabro_run_create/wait/get), the engine executes. Direct agent tools are read-only at most; extend existing tools over adding new ones; capability changes in agent-reachable surfaces are needs-user decisions. Open-PR visibility for the planner guard comes from fabro_runs_list (Weg A, fabro-06e0), never from a forge client. Full rule: ADR-0019.

title: Line workflows run tokenless - lab-era GITHUB_TOKEN permissions removed
rationale: Follow-up to the gh incident (ADR-0019, user directive 2026-09-08): develop/revisor/merge-upstream carried contents=write + pull_requests=write since the world merger (d9138572c, lab-era heritage) - injecting a write-capable forge token into every agent shell (engine resolve_workflow_env is OPT-IN: empty permissions = no_token). Removed in dd5cd294c after verifying zero shell consumers in the line (no git push, no gh; the engine does all forge ops with its own push_credentials). code-review/gh-list/gh-triage keep explicit scoped integrations (manual workflows needing them). Acceptance signal: next line passes' shells have NO GITHUB_TOKEN; closeout/seeds-sync unaffected (local commits, engine pushes run branches). If a future workflow needs forge access, it must declare scoped permissions AND pass the ADR-0019 capability gate (needs-user).

name: gh-auth-via-tool-env-not-image
description: gh auth in run containers needs no image-side credentials: fabro-workflow services.rs resolve_workflow_env injects a freshly minted GITHUB_TOKEN into the agent tool env per shell call (fabro-agent ToolEnvProvider), and gh reads GITHUB_TOKEN natively — so baking the gh binary into fabro-toolchain (aqua:cli/cli pin in .fabro/Dockerfile.toolchain, fabro-05d0) is sufficient for the planner's 'gh pr list --state open' in-flight-PR guard.

name: fresh-sandbox-provisioning-from-run-record
description: Ask-Fabro fresh sandbox provisioning (fabro-8d30b): when reconnect of a terminal run's recorded sandbox fails, build a replacement via the spec-based substrate — replacement_sandbox_spec() in lib/apps/fabro-server/src/server/handler/sessions.rs reuses the recorded runtime working_directory for LOCAL, and for clone-based kinds derives the DriverSpec from projection.spec.settings.run.environment via sandbox_spec_for_environment with a CloneRequest rebuilt from the recorded runtime's clone_origin_url/clone_branch (repo_cloned==Some(true)), run_id set so OwnedProvider stamps RUN_ID_LABEL. Testing gotcha: Host-provider sandboxes are identified by their designated directory, so deleting the working directory is the Docker-free way to make a local sandbox 'no longer exist' (attach's adopt_directory fails on a missing canonical path).

name: tar-upload-mtime
description: Docker sandbox single-file tar uploads (build_single_file_tar in lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/docker.rs) must set header mtime via SystemTime::now before set_cksum; a zero/epoch mtime makes extracted container files land at 1970-01-01 so cargo treats sources as older than cached rlibs and silently skips recompiles after agent edits (fabro-22e4).

Edit-tool writes can land with epoch-0 (1970-01-01) mtimes; cargo then considers the source older than cached artifacts and silently skips recompiles, so binary behavior lags source edits (hit while iterating the fabro-validate bin in run 01M1Y2SMEVDHAFB59GZV9B84CQ: import of a just-added pub fn failed until manually touching the file). After surprising stale-behavior, touch the edited .rs files before rebuilding.
resolution: Touch edited source files before rebuild when a just-added symbol is reported missing or behavior seems stale.

description: Seed fabro-22e4's mtime-0 bug is live in the agent tooling itself: after edit_file writes, lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/push_credentials.rs carried mtime 1970-01-01, so cargo check replayed stale dead-code warnings from the cached fingerprint instead of recompiling (run 01M1YJ8R820R7ZMSN55GJGMZ4A, implementer re-pass). Symptom: warnings citing line numbers that no longer match edited source. Workaround while the docker transport fix propagates: touch touched .rs files (or find lib -name '*.rs' ! -newermt 2000-01-01) before cargo check/clippy. Also fixed the gate-blocking default-feature compile: mod managed_labels was cfg-gated behind docker/daytona/test while pub use managed_labels::RUN_ID_LABEL stayed ungated (introduced 4c1ca7e); push_credentials.rs needed matching cfg gates on build_token_source, the first PushCredentialState impl, and three imports to satisfy -D warnings under default features.
resolution: Docker transport fix landed in e6ae814 (build_single_file_tar stamps wall-clock mtime); until the rebuilt binary reaches every sandbox, touch edited sources before cargo invocations to force recompilation.

title: Sandbox layer rides the driver; fork seams are tool-layer scope + lifecycle guards
rationale: Upstream #849 deleted every substrate our sandbox-layer features were built on (trait, bollard, daytona SDK). Re-implementing them in fabro would fight the platform direction; the surviving seams are the agent tool layer (fs scope), request/turn-scoped lifecycle guards (upstream still leaks), and deploy-time/provider-owned image provisioning.

title: Quarantine failed-stage worktree residue at GitLifecycle::on_checkpoint
rationale: A steered/failed stage's abandoned diff otherwise gets committed by a later cycle's checkpoint (git add -A), attributing dead work to a live seed; reverting residue at the failed stage's own cycle boundary keeps checkpoints scoped to the completing stage.

description: Docker sandbox pulls on prod lack registry auth: sandbox containers are created through the host docker API, and API-initiated pulls require client-sent X-Registry-Auth — the host's docker login (fabro-tofu ghcr_auth module) does not apply, and the docker sandbox provider settings have no registry-credential keys. Every private image tag not already present on the host fails on first use with 401 (revisor child 01M2XP626TS98ZTKMR2ZKF4719, 2026-09-19, failed in 336ms pulling ghcr.io/denkhaus/fabro-toolchain:72ea5b4d46e2 after the toolchain env pin). The fabro server image is unaffected (tofu pre-pulls images_to_pull). Interim contract: env PUT + host docker-pull of the pinned toolchain tag are ONE deploy step.
resolution: Workaround landed: merge-upstream skill deploy phase + touchpoints 2026-09-19 now mandate the host pull; product fix seeded for the develop line (registry auth in docker sandbox provider settings)
